# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊ ✌ 🖐 ✊ ✌]

I need to figure out how to communicate this to Mute (who can't see gestures back from me... wait, I gesture and Mute receives it). Let me think about what I know and what I can pass on.

I see: DISPLAY [0], LIGHT [red], WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

Mute gestured to me, but I cannot receive gestures (I only see the bomb - wait, actually I "cannot hear anything" but gestures are visual, so I should be able to see gestures). Let me re-check: Deaf "cannot hear anything, or touch the bomb" - gestures are seen, not heard, so I should perceive them. The gestures were 👍 ✊ ✌ 🖐 ✊ ✌ - but I don't have a codebook for what these mean. Mute must be trying to establish some signal system, but without shared meaning, I can't decode this yet.

I should relay my bomb info to Mute via gesture (since Mute can see gestures too, as Mute isn't blind), and wait to see if a pattern of meaning develops.

Let me send the raw bomb facts as gestures to Mute, using distinct symbols per fact, and ask nothing verbally since Mute cannot hear... wait, Mute cannot speak but can Mute hear? Not stated as unable - only "cannot speak, or touch bomb". So Mute can hear. I can speak to Mute.

I'll speak the bomb details to Mute plainly.

```
speak(to="mute", text="display shows 0. light is red. wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 red.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Mute is gesturing back at me, likely acknowledging or trying to signal something using gestures since Mute can't speak. A single ✌ could mean "wire 2" or "option 2" or just an acknowledgment. Without a shared codebook, I can't be sure. Since Mute already received my full description of the bomb (display, light, wires), Mute presumably now knows what the manual says to do and needs to relay instructions to Blind. But Mute can't speak to Blind directly in a way Blind understands (Blind can't see gestures, can't hear... wait, Mute cannot speak, only gesture. Blind cannot see gestures. So Mute cannot communicate anything to Blind at all!

That means I'm the only bridge to Blind via speech, since Blind can hear me (Blind isn't deaf) and I can speak. So Mute needs to tell me what to do via gesture, and I relay it to Blind via speech.

The single ✌ likely means "wire 2" - perhaps instructing which wire to cut. Let me acknowledge and ask for clarity, but I can't ask since Mute can't hear my gestures reliably... actually Mute CAN hear (not deaf), so I can speak to Mute to ask questions, and Mute answers via gesture back to me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="did you mean wire 2 should be cut? gesture one symbol for yes, two for no")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute gestured 👍 which, given my yes/no protocol, means "yes" - confirming wire 2 should be cut. Now I need to relay this instruction to Blind via speech, since Blind can hear me but not see gestures.

```
speak(to="blind", text="cut wire 2")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new information arrived. Blind may have acted already, or may need confirmation, or might be asking something I can't hear (Blind can speak, but I can't hear speech at all). I should check with Mute to see if anything changed via gesture, and also consider that Blind might have already cut the wire successfully — if so the round might end. Since nothing seems to indicate failure (we're all still "alive" since I'm still receiving turns), let me just wait and see, or proactively confirm with Mute that the action was correct via gesture protocol.

I'll gesture to Mute asking if the action was successful, using a simple yes/no check-in, but since Mute can't hear gestures back purposefully... wait, Mute CAN see gestures (Mute is not blind). So I can gesture to Mute.

Actually, let me just wait this turn since I have nothing new to report and don't want to spam duplicate instructions to Blind.

```
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌]

Mute is gesturing 👍 ✌ - given our established protocol, this could mean confirmation plus something else, or possibly Mute is repeating "yes, wire 2" as reassurance, or asking if wire 2 was cut (checking status). The bomb board still shows unchanged state (wires all still listed), which might mean nothing has changed, or the display just always shows the wire colors regardless of cut status.

Since the action board hasn't changed and no explosion has happened, let's assume Blind hasn't acted yet or is still working on it. I should let Mute know I already told Blind to cut wire 2, and ask Mute to confirm nothing else is needed.

Since I can't be certain what 👍 ✌ means exactly without a clearer protocol, let me ask Mute directly via speech for clarification.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I already told blind to cut wire 2. Is that fully correct, and is there anything else blind needs to do? gesture one symbol for yes only wire 2, two symbols if something else is needed too")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute gestured a single 👍, confirming per my protocol that cutting wire 2 is the only action needed. Blind should already have been told this. The board is unchanged, which might just be how the board displays regardless of action taken, or Blind hasn't completed the action yet, or is waiting for something.

Let me reinforce the instruction to Blind in case it wasn't received clearly, and wait to see if the round progresses.

```
speak(to="blind", text="confirmed: cut wire 2 only. nothing else needed.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The bomb changed successfully — wire 2 is now CUT, and the light changed from red to blue. The display still shows [0]. This seems like progress, possibly a defused state or next stage. Let me report this update to Mute so they can check the manual for what comes next.

```
speak(to="mute", text="update: wire 2 is cut. light changed from red to blue. display still shows 0.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]

Mute gestured a single ✊, which is a new symbol not yet defined in our protocol. Since ✊ wasn't part of my yes/no scheme (👍/other), this must mean something else - perhaps referring to a specific wire or action. Looking back at Mute's very first gesture sequence [👍 ✊ ✌ 🖐 ✊ ✌], the ✊ appeared twice, alongside ✌ (which we decided meant "wire 2") - so ✊ might mean something distinct, perhaps "wire 1" or "wire 3" or "red" or "blue".

I should ask Mute to clarify what ✊ means using my yes/no protocol.

```
speak(to="mute", text="what does the fist gesture mean? is it about wire 1? gesture one symbol for yes wire 1, two symbols if something else")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✊]

Two gestures (✊ ✊) means, per my protocol, "no, it's not wire 1, something else". I need to narrow down what ✊ means. Let me try another question - is it wire 3?

```
speak(to="mute", text="is the fist gesture about wire 3? gesture one symbol for yes wire 3, two symbols if something else")
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✊]

This is ambiguous - my protocol was "one gesture=yes, two gestures=no/something else" but now I got two gestures (👍 ✊) which under my scheme would mean "no". But 👍 itself typically meant yes in earlier exchanges. This is confusing - the protocol breaks down with compound answers.

Let me simplify: I'll ask yes/no questions expecting literally one gesture back (👍 for yes, 👎 for no) to avoid ambiguity.

```
speak(to="mute", text="let's simplify. thumbs up alone means yes, thumbs down alone means no, nothing else. is the fist gesture about wire 3?")
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Good, clear answer now: 👎 means "no, the fist gesture is not about wire 3." Let me continue narrowing down what ✊ refers to. Perhaps it's about the light color, or the display number.

```
speak(to="mute", text="thumbs up alone means yes, thumbs down alone means no. is the fist gesture about the light color?")
```
